title: Trace handoff negotiator with health smoothing for multi-backend exports
creator: Alyssa Chen
description: Build a negotiator layer in the trace ingest path that selects and hands off spans to the appropriate backend (Tempo, Jaeger-compatible sinks, and cold-archive S3) using a health-smoothing algorithm. The goal is to avoid flapping between backends during transient backend degradation, maintain ordered delivery guarantees where possible, and expose decisioning metrics for SLO and on-call resolution. The negotiator should sit after standard OTLP normalization and before per-tenant exporter adapters so it can: 1) consult backend health signals, 2) apply a smoothing window and hysteresis, 3) apply tenant routing policy (static mapping, weighted fallback), and 4) emit a trace-handoff event for downstream observability and audits.
acceptance_criteria: Negotiator routes >99.9% of spans to primary backend when primary is healthy by our health definition
When primary backend degrades, negotiator shifts routing using a 60-120s smoothing window rather than immediate failover
Decision metrics (chosen_backend, backend_health_score, smoothing_state, latency_ms) are emitted to metrics pipeline and visible in the tracing console
Ordering preserved for in-flight spans within a tenant lane when switching backends where backend supports ordered acks
Unit and e2e tests cover simulated backend flaps and verify no data duplication or silent drops beyond configured retention policy
Feature toggle + canary rollout plan exists with override API for emergency operator control
comments: 2025-11-04 - Triage: flagged as high priority after incident INC-2025-11-02 where Tempo saw intermittent fullshard GC and clients experienced flapping. Suggested spike to reduce blast radius for tenant failovers.

2025-11-12 - Design spike complete: evaluated three approaches (immediate failover, token-bucket gate, and health-smoothing with hysteresis). Chosen: health-smoothing with configurable window and explicit state machine. Rationale: minimizes false positives and syncs with autoscaler timescales.

2025-11-20 - Prototype: implemented smoothing state machine and a pluggable backend-health adapter. Basic metrics emitted: backend_health_score (0-100), chosen_backend, smoothing_state. Integration test harness simulates backend latency and error rates.
2026-01-15 - Review feedback from PM (Jorge Alvarez): add per-tenant override table and audit events for compliance. Also requested TLS policy check for legacy Jaeger adapters.
2026-02-02 - Security review: cryptographic handshake and credential rotation for exporter credentials validated by security. No blockers, minor note to audit long-lived tokens used by archive sink.
2026-02-24 - PR opened (trace-ingest#4621). Initial CI failing on flaky e2e due to timing of smoothing window; added deterministic clock to tests and reduced nondeterminism.
2026-03-03 - QA notes: staging load test with synthetic flapping backend passed at smoothing_window=90s, but tenant with high QPS observed queue growth; follow-up to tune backpressure thresholds.

2026-03-09 - Canaries: enabled for 10% of tenants in production with monitoring dashboard panels added. No customer-facing errors observed; oncall acknowledged small increase in export latency which is within SLA.
Next steps: finalize runbook entries, add automatic fallback escalation when smoothing state persists beyond threshold, and schedule post-mortem readiness review with SRE team.
rollout_plan: Stage: feature flag off by default. Canary on 10% tenants for 48h with automated rollback if exported-latency>200ms or dropped-span-rate>0.05%. Gradual ramp to 100% over two weeks. Provide override API for SRE. Backpressure thresholds configurable per-tenant.
testing_plan: Unit tests for state transitions, deterministic clock harness for smoothing windows, chaos tests simulating backend GC pauses, e2e with mock exporters asserting no dupes and ordering guarantees, and load test at 2x production QPS for a representative tenant lane.
implementation_notes: Negotiator implemented as a stateless decision layer that emits idempotent handoff events. Uses backend health score aggregator from telemetry (dashboards) plus realtime probe pings as fallback. Persistence of transient handoff decisions uses a short-lived in-memory cache (TTL ~5m) with optional redis-backed sticky mapping for durable handoffs in Dedicated deployments.
